about: Stages and timing for the onsite-test playbook. scripts/handoff.py reads this file: the stages it tracks, the outcomes each stage can record, and how long to wait between stages. Each key is explained under notes.

stages.name: find
stages.do: Audit the project's weblayers and web experiments, add the ones worth testing (never tested, poor results) as findings, and ask the user which to test.

stages.name: build
stages.do: Write the challenger's weblayer code for the user to paste into an inactive copy of the weblayer (or a new inactive weblayer) in the Engagement UI, with the Smart triggering conditions to set.

skip_when.reason: the find stage found nothing worth testing.

stages.name: qa
stages.do: QA the inactive weblayer until it is GO; a NO-GO fix goes back through the build stage's skill (engagement-weblayer-builder) and the user pastes it. Then wait for the user to launch the A/B test in the Engagement UI, record the day it started, and record the launch as a change (source engagement-ui).

skip_when.reason: the find stage found nothing worth testing.

stages.name: read-out
stages.do: Read the test's result on the agreed metric. Don't stop early on a good-looking day.

skip_when.reason: the find stage found nothing worth testing.
the qa stage was skipped, so no launch was recorded.

notes.min_test_days: Days after the qa stage finishes (the day the user launched the test) before the read-out is due. engagement-experiment-readout calls a winner only after at least 14 days in whole weeks; use the planned end date when it's later.
notes.wait_outcomes: Outcomes that mean a stage isn't finished yet. The script records them only with status in_progress and a --not-before date to come back on, so status never shows the stage as due before then. no_winner is the way out of a test that never becomes conclusive.
notes.playbooks: Each playbook's title, product and stages in order. A stage names the skill that does it, whether that skill writes, what to do, the outcomes it can record, not_before (wait this rules key's number of days after another stage is done) and skip_when (suggest skipping when another stage had one of these outcomes, or with skipped: true when it was skipped; skips don't cascade, so each stage lists every earlier outcome that ends the run). Every stage skill is read-only: engagement-weblayer-builder returns code the user pastes, and the user creates the weblayer copy, sets the split and launches it in the Engagement UI, so the playbook is read-only and the launch is recorded as a change with source engagement-ui. The test is the weblayer's own A/B split (challenger against the original, or a Control group); engagement-experiment-readout reads weblayer splits from banner events when asked, and web experiments from search_experiments. The find stage can be skipped when the user brings their own test idea. A scenario A/B test can be set up with engagement-ab-test-setup when the change is a message rather than an on-site experience; it isn't a stage.
